correctness.rationale: The pair Casimirs give a shift B+Kk, where B=−3mK/4 and k is the number of triplets. The hub interaction is J/2 times j(j+1)−s(s+1)−3/4, where s is the combined triplet spin. It gives the two stated branches, with only the upper branch at s=0. The weight-count difference in the spin-one tensor power gives the multiplicities; including hub spin and the triplet choices exhausts dimension 2·4^m. At k≥1 the unique maximal-spin representation per pair choice has s=k, j=k−1/2 and energy e_k=B+k(K−J/2)−J/2. Minimizing the affine positive-k sequence against e_0=B verifies all five regions; each minimizing k≥1 contributes 2k times the number of pair choices. At K=J/2 this gives m2^m, hence the stated entropy per physical spin. Any different level within a fixed k≥1 is at least J/2 above e_k. Off the crossings, the neighboring affine minimum (when lower than the all-singlet competitor) or e_0/e_1 gives the stated gaps, all less than J/2 or below the next positive-k competitor. At the lower crossing e_0 attains the J/2 separation; at the upper crossing e_2 attains it and exists because m≥2.
residual_risks: First distinct means above the entire ground space; the gap at a crossing is not the limiting separation of branches approaching the crossing. The model assumes isotropic exchange, a uniform hub and uniform pair bonds.
